h1:
Roi Et to Khon Kaen
A Central Isan Road Trip
intro: Roi Et and Khon Kaen are two of central Isan's main cities, and they sit on the same line. From downtown Roi Et to downtown Khon Kaen is about 113 km along Highway 23 (Chaeng Sanit Road), passing through Maha Sarakham in the middle, and it takes roughly an hour and a half to two hours. A lot of people fly or take the train into Khon Kaen and stay there, when a short drive down toward Roi Et gets you the 101 Tower (a city-view tower with a zipline), the lake of Bueng Phlan Chai in the center of town, and the Great Buddha at Wat Burapha Phiram. This plan runs 2 days and 1 night: day one covers the Roi Et highlights and then moves up to overnight in Khon Kaen, and day two takes in Bueng Kaen Nakhon, the 9-tier Phra That Kaen Nakhon, and a few cafes in town, all with real timings and routes you can drive yourself.

blocks.html: What makes this trip work is that the two cities have different characters but are only an hour and a half apart by car. Roi Et is a small, compact town you can see almost entirely on foot, with Bueng Phlan Chai in the center paired with the new 101 Tower landmark, a calm feel, and cheap eats. Khon Kaen is the biggest city in central Isan, with Bueng Kaen Nakhon lake, the 9-tier Phra Maha That Kaen Nakhon, a dinosaur museum, and a whole crop of new cafes around Khon Kaen University. Putting them together over two days gives you both the slow small town and the busy big city in one trip.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: This trip is easiest with your own car, because the main Roi Et to Khon Kaen route is a straight run along Highway 23 through Maha Sarakham in the middle. The sights in each city are fairly spread out, especially Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon in Roi Et's Nong Phok district, which is another 80 km or so out from town. If you don't have a private car, renting one from Khon Kaen or Roi Et airport and driving yourself keeps you on schedule far better. Budget for fuel and around 120 to 150 km of driving per day.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Roi Et highlights, then up to Khon Kaen

blocks.html: Day one starts in downtown Roi Et from morning into the afternoon, covering Bueng Phlan Chai, the 101 Tower, and the Great Buddha at Wat Burapha Phiram, all of which are in town and walkable to one another. Then you drive up to overnight in Khon Kaen in the evening, so the next morning you can start exploring Khon Kaen straight away without backtracking. The route from Roi Et up to Khon Kaen uses Highway 23 through Maha Sarakham, an easy drive the whole way.

items.activity: Start at Bueng Phlan Chai in central Roi Et
items.note: A lake in the middle of town covering around 50 rai, with an island in the center, the city pillar shrine, and a large walking-pose Buddha. Come early before the sun gets harsh and the loop around the lake is an easy walk. It's a fitting place to open the trip, right in the city center. One side of the lake is Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park, where the tower stands.

items.activity: Climb the 101 Tower for a 360-degree city view
items.note: A city-view tower about 101 meters tall in Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park, right next to Bueng Phlan Chai. Up top you see Roi Et in every direction, and there's a city museum, a coffee shop, and a zipline off the tower to try. Check the opening times and admission on their page before you go, as they adjust seasonally.

items.activity: Pay respects to the Great Buddha at Wat Burapha Phiram
items.note: A temple in Roi Et town with a very tall blessing-pose Buddha you can spot from far away, a city icon that locals revere. It's a few minutes' walk or drive from Bueng Phlan Chai. Stop to make merit and take photos before lunch.

items.activity: Lunch, Isan style, in Roi Et town
items.note: Roi Et is Thung Kula jasmine rice country. Try rice with laab, koi, som tam, grilled chicken, or bamboo-shoot soup at a local spot around Bueng Phlan Chai. It's easy on the wallet. Fuel up, then drive north.

items.activity: Drive Roi Et → Khon Kaen ~113 km
items.note: Take Highway 23 (Chaeng Sanit Road) through Maha Sarakham in the middle, about an hour and a half to two hours to reach downtown Khon Kaen. It's the main road and an easy drive, with Isan rice-field views the whole way. If you're hungry there are petrol stations and roadside spots along the way, or you can stop in Maha Sarakham for a break.

items.activity: Check in to your Khon Kaen stay, wander the city
items.note: Khon Kaen is a big city, with stays ranging from budget chain hotels to large hotels in the center. Pick a spot near Bueng Kaen Nakhon or Si Chan Road and dinner is easy to find. Rest up from the drive, then head out to eat.

items.activity: Dinner and a cafe around Khon Kaen University
items.note: Khon Kaen has plenty of food. The Kang Sadan area and the streets around Khon Kaen University are packed with restaurants and new-wave cafes. Try mu thup (pounded dried pork) or Isan sausage, both local favorites. Close out day one with a relaxed cafe before heading back to your stay.

blocks.title: Where to stay tonight
blocks.html: Staying in Khon Kaen tonight is the most convenient option, since you can start exploring Khon Kaen first thing the next morning. Khon Kaen is a big city with far more accommodation choices than Roi Et, from budget chain hotels to large hotels attached to shopping centers. Pick somewhere central or near Bueng Kaen Nakhon and you can easily walk to food and cafes.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Bueng Kaen Nakhon, the 9-tier stupa, and Khon Kaen cafes

blocks.html: Day two is mostly spent in Khon Kaen city. Start at Bueng Kaen Nakhon paired with Wat Nong Waeng, home to the 9-tier Phra Maha That Kaen Nakhon. Go to the top floor and you see the whole lake and the city. If you have more time, add the Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum out to the west, then catch a cafe and some souvenirs before driving back.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Explore Khon Kaen, then head back

items.activity: Bueng Kaen Nakhon and Wat Nong Waeng, the 9-tier Phra That Kaen Nakhon
items.note: A large lake in central Khon Kaen. On the shore sits Wat Nong Waeng with the 9-tier Phra Maha That Kaen Nakhon, in a Dvaravati-Indochinese style. Climb to the top floor and you see the lake and the city all around. Come early before the sun gets harsh for an easy walk, and make merit as you wish.

items.activity: Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum (if you have time)
items.note: Out in Wiang Kao district to the west of the city, about an hour and a half drive away. It displays dinosaur skeletons excavated at Phu Wiang, good for those with time to spare and traveling with kids. If your schedule is tight or you're heading back this evening, skip it and focus on the city instead.

Khon Kaen has lots of Isan and made-to-order spots. The Si Chan Road area and around Bueng Kaen Nakhon are easy to find. Try kaeng om, laab, or Vietnamese-style kuai chap, a local Isan staple, before picking up souvenirs.

Before heading back, stop at a cafe around Kang Sadan or near the university, and pick up Isan souvenirs like mu thup, sausage, naem, and silk in town. It's a nice way to close the trip before you set off.

items.activity: Drive back to Roi Et, or continue on
items.note: From Khon Kaen back to Roi Et it's the same route, about an hour and a half to two hours. If you're flying out of Khon Kaen airport, an early-afternoon departure from the city works out nicely. Stop in Maha Sarakham along the way if you have time.

blocks.text: Sights not to miss in both provinces

items.name: 101 Tower (Roi Et)
items.blurb: A city-view tower about 101 meters tall in Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park, next to Bueng Phlan Chai. From the top you see Roi Et in every direction, and there's a city museum, a coffee shop, and a zipline off the tower. It's the new landmark and the main highlight on the Roi Et side.
items.meta: In Roi Et town · admission applies, check times before going

items.name: Bueng Kaen Nakhon and the 9-tier Phra That Kaen Nakhon (Khon Kaen)
items.blurb: A large lake in central Khon Kaen with the 9-tier Phra Maha That Kaen Nakhon at Wat Nong Waeng. Climb to the top floor and you see the whole lake and city. It's a spot where you get both merit-making and a city view in one place, the main highlight on the Khon Kaen side.
items.meta: Central Khon Kaen · make merit as you wish

items.name: Bueng Phlan Chai (Roi Et)
items.blurb: A lake in the center of Roi Et covering around 50 rai, with an island, the city pillar shrine, and a large walking-pose Buddha. It's a public park where locals come to walk and exercise, and a fitting place to open a Roi Et trip.
items.meta: In Roi Et town · free entry

items.name: Wat Burapha Phiram and the Great Buddha (Roi Et)
items.blurb: A temple in Roi Et town with a very tall blessing-pose Buddha you can spot from far away, a city icon that locals revere. It's near Bueng Phlan Chai, so it's easy to drop by for some merit-making.
items.meta: In Roi Et town · free entry

items.name: Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon (Roi Et)
items.blurb: A large white-and-gold chedi about 101 meters tall at Wat Pha Nam Thip Thep Prasit Wararam in Nong Phok district. It sits on a hill and is visible from far off, with intricate detailing inside and out. It's about 80 km from Roi Et town, good if you can add another day.
items.meta: Nong Phok district · ~80 km from town

items.name: Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum (Khon Kaen)
items.blurb: A museum displaying dinosaur skeletons and fossils excavated at Phu Wiang, out in Wiang Kao district to the west of the city, about an hour and a half drive away. Great for traveling with kids and anyone who loves dinosaurs.
items.meta: Wiang Kao district, Khon Kaen · admission applies

blocks.text: What to eat along the way

blocks.html: This route is solid Isan-food territory, with local dishes easy to find in both cities. Roi Et is the land of Thung Kula Rong Hai jasmine rice, so the rice here is fragrant to begin with, while Khon Kaen is a big city with more variety and plenty of new-wave cafes. If you pass through Maha Sarakham in between, it's an easy place to stop and eat.

items: Thung Kula jasmine rice (Roi Et) — the famous fragrant rice of Thung Kula Rong Hai, eaten with laab, koi, som tam, and grilled chicken at local spots around Bueng Phlan Chai. Easy on the wallet.
Local Isan dishes — laab, koi, jaew, bamboo-shoot soup, and kaeng om are easy to find in every market across Roi Et, Maha Sarakham, and Khon Kaen, with a bold, genuinely local flavor.
Mu thup and Isan sausage (Khon Kaen) — a famous Khon Kaen snack and souvenir, sold at souvenir shops in town and easy to take home.
Cafes around Khon Kaen University — the Kang Sadan area and the streets around Khon Kaen University have lots of new-wave cafes, easy spots to rest or get some work done mid-trip.

Roi Et → Khon Kaen — about 113 km on Highway 23 (Chaeng Sanit Road) through Maha Sarakham in the middle, around an hour and a half to two hours driving yourself. It's the main road and an easy drive, and there are intercity buses and minivans too if you don't have a private car.

Stop in Maha Sarakham in the middle — Maha Sarakham sits right at the midpoint of the route, so if you have time you can stop at Wat Pa Wang Nam Yen or break for a meal along the way without going out of your way.

In Roi Et town — Bueng Phlan Chai, the 101 Tower, and Wat Burapha Phiram are all in town and walkable to one another, while Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon is out in Nong Phok district about 80 km away, so allow another half day for it.

Flights and trains — both Roi Et and Khon Kaen have airports, and Khon Kaen has more frequent flights plus a train station. Many people fly into Khon Kaen, rent a car, and drive down to Roi Et following this plan.

blocks.title: Pacing the time right
blocks.html: If you only have 2 days and 1 night, focus on the in-town sights on both sides: Bueng Phlan Chai, the 101 Tower, and the Great Buddha on the Roi Et side, plus Bueng Kaen Nakhon and the 9-tier Phra That Kaen Nakhon on the Khon Kaen side, and skip the far-off spots like Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon and the Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum for now. If you want to fit in those two distant spots as well, stretch it to 3 days and 2 nights so you're not rushing the drives.

blocks.text: Tweak the plan to your style

items.name: Temple and merit-making
items.blurb: Focus on the Great Buddha at Wat Burapha Phiram and the 9-tier Phra That Kaen Nakhon, then add Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon in Nong Phok if you can spare a day. You'll cover the city icons of both provinces.

items.name: City and cafes
items.blurb: Take in Bueng Phlan Chai and the 101 Tower on the Roi Et side, then focus on the cafes around Khon Kaen University and Bueng Kaen Nakhon. Relaxed walking in both cities, no long drives.

items.name: Family
items.blurb: Add the Phu Wiang Dinosaur Museum so the kids can see dinosaur skeletons, climb the 101 Tower for the view, and schedule frequent breaks since the driving distances are fairly long.

faq.q: Are Roi Et and Khon Kaen far apart? Can you visit them back to back?
faq.a: Not very far. From downtown Roi Et to downtown Khon Kaen is about 113 km, roughly an hour and a half to two hours by car on Highway 23 through Maha Sarakham in the middle. The two are central Isan's main cities on the same line, so a back-to-back 2-day, 1-night trip fits nicely.

faq.q: What is the 101 Tower, and what do you see from the top?
faq.a: The 101 Tower is a city-view tower about 101 meters tall in Somdet Phra Srinagarindra Park, next to Bueng Phlan Chai in central Roi Et. From the top you get a 360-degree view of the city in every direction, and inside there's a city museum, a coffee shop, and a zipline off the tower. There's an admission fee, and it's worth checking opening times and ticket prices on their page before you go, as they adjust seasonally.

faq.q: Can you do this trip without a private car?
faq.a: You can, but it's less convenient. The Roi Et to Khon Kaen route has intercity buses and minivans, but the sights within each city are spread out, especially Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkhon in Nong Phok district, which is far and hard to reach by public transport. If you don't have a car, renting one from Khon Kaen or the airport and driving yourself keeps you on schedule far better.

faq.q: Which city should you stay in, Roi Et or Khon Kaen?
faq.a: With this plan, one night in Khon Kaen is the most convenient, since you cover Roi Et over the morning and afternoon of day one, then drive up to overnight in Khon Kaen and continue exploring Khon Kaen the next morning without backtracking. Khon Kaen is a big city with far more accommodation choices than Roi Et, from budget chain hotels to large hotels in the center.

faq.q: What's the best time of year to go?
faq.a: The cool season, roughly November to February, has lovely weather, so walking around the lakes and temples and climbing the tower outdoors is comfortable without being too hot. If your trip lines up with Roi Et's Bun Phawet festival around March, it's especially lively, as it's the city's big merit-making festival.
